summary: Kickoff meeting for BeaconMed onboarding to Redwood Inference. Reviewed scope of implementation (pilot for patient triage assistant), deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security requirements (SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs), staging access and initial timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send docs and schedule SE deep dive; BeaconMed to provide pilot user list and staging access info.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (CSM): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Happy Friday. Quick round of intros then we'll go through the kickoff agenda.
[00:00:07] Dr. Laura Kim: Hi, Laura here, Head of AI at BeaconMed. Nice to meet you all.
[00:00:10] Sam Torres: Sam, engineering lead on the triage team.
[00:00:13] Janelle Morris: Janelle, security and compliance.
[00:00:15] Victor Alvarez: Victor, product.
[00:00:17] Ethan (SE): Ethan from Redwood, solutions engineer. Hi all.
[00:00:20] Ravi (Platform): Ravi, platform eng at Redwood, will help with VPC/networking stuff.
[00:00:25] Maya: Cool. Agenda: project goals, scope of pilot, technical integration points, security & compliance checklist, timeline, owners. Any extra items?
[00:00:33] Sam: No, that covers it for us.
[00:00:35] Maya: Great. Laura, could you kick us off with goals and success criteria?
[00:00:40] Dr. Laura Kim: Sure. Our main goal is to launch a constrained pilot for the patient triage assistant — basically text-based symptom intake. Key success is accuracy and latency under 600ms p95 for typical sessions, and also not to exceed a cost of X per 1k interactions. We'll start with a 2-week pilot involving engineering and product. If that looks good, we want Dedicated reserved capacity by Q3.
[00:01:00] Maya: Perfect, thank you. That helps scope. Ethan, can you summarize integration options?
[00:01:06] Ethan: Yeah. There's three typical paths: 1) Hosted Redwood API — fastest to go live, we manage infra; 2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput; 3) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) — for strict data residency and network isolation. For a pilot we usually recommend hosted to validate prompts and evals, then move to Dedicated or Private for production depending on requirements.
[00:01:30] Sam: We're leaning Dedicated if latency and data isolation are good. Also want SSO and audit logs.
[00:01:36] Ethan: Totally — Dedicated supports an isolated GPU pool plus private networking and can integrate with your KMS for key management. 
[00:01:44] Janelle: On compliance, SOC 2 and audit logs are non-negotiable. We also need SAML SSO, RBAC for user roles, and the ability to keep logs for 12 months. How do you handle KMS and log retention?
[00:01:57] Ravi: We can integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). Audit logs are available both in the Console and via log export; retention length is configurable in Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we keep shorter retention by default but enterprise add-on can extend it.
[00:02:12] Janelle: Okay, that sounds promising. A few of our legal folks will ask about egress and data residency too.
[00:02:17] Maya: We'll share our security pack with SOC2 certs and SOC audits, and the SAML/SSO doc. We'll also include Dedicated/networking diagrams.
[00:02:25] Dr. Laura Kim: Great. On the technical side, Sam, what's your team's stack and existing infra?
[00:02:31] Sam: We're mostly on AWS, microservices in EKS, and we have an internal API gateway. For the triage app we have a staging cluster and a message bus. We'll need to route requests through our gateway to Redwood endpoints. We prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink for Dedicated.
[00:02:45] Ethan: VPC peering is supported; we also have options for PrivateLink depending on region. For initial pilot, many teams use API keys with IP allow-listing and then switch to VPC when moving to Dedicated.
[00:02:57] Victor: We also have HL7-adjacent PII concerns — we want to make sure we have clear encryption in transit and at rest, and that Redwood doesn't store PII unless configured.
[00:03:06] Ravi: By default we don't retain conversations beyond configured retention windows unless you're using features that require storage. We can also enable prefix/KV cache retention policies or disable caching for sensitive data. Apologies, I said KV "cash" earlier in the last demo — I mean KV cache.
[00:03:20] (laughter)
[00:03:22] Janelle: Haha, noted. We'll want to see the configuration options. Also need details on data deletion and audit log formats.
[00:03:30] Maya: We'll add that to the security pack. I'll put it in the action items.
[00:03:33] Dr. Laura Kim: About performance — our SLA target for pilot is p95 < 600ms. You mentioned batching and caching help with cost; will that affect latency?
[00:03:42] Ethan: Good question. Intelligent batching can improve throughput and unit cost but will add a small queuing delay. For low-latency interactive use cases we tune batch windows aggressively and use prefix/KV caching for repeated context. For Dedicated we can reserve more instances to meet p95 targets. We'll propose a perf plan in the SE deep dive.
[00:03:58] Sam: We'll want to run a benchmark with our typical session distribution. Can Redwood run a benchmark against our prompt set?
[00:04:04] Ethan: Yes, we can. We'll need a sanitized prompt set and sample traffic patterns. We can run tests in a staging environment or run a controlled load test against hosted endpoints.
[00:04:13] Sam: Ok we'll prepare that.
[00:04:15] Janelle: For SSO, we use Okta. Do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning?
[00:04:20] Maya: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in enterprise plans. We'll send the SSO guide and sample metadata.
[00:04:27] Janelle: Good. Also need to confirm encryption-at-rest with customer KMS.
[00:04:31] Ravi: Yes — customer-managed KMS supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted can integrate with partner KMS for enterprise.
[00:04:38] Victor: Timeline — what's a realistic timeline for pilot and then Dedicated?
[00:04:42] Maya: Typical timeline: 1-2 weeks to onboard and validate prompts on hosted, 2-4 weeks for pilot depending on performance and compliance checks, then Dedicated provisioning can take 2-6 weeks depending on contract and capacity. For BeaconMed given SOC2 and VPC needs, I'd budget 6-8 weeks to move to Dedicated after pilot signoff.
[00:04:58] Dr. Laura Kim: That aligns with our Q3 target.
[00:05:01] Maya: Next, responsibilities: Redwood will provide onboarding docs, security pack, and run initial perf baseline. BeaconMed to provide prompt corpus, staging access, and pilot user list. SE to schedule deep dive to design VPC/PrivateLink and perf plan.
[00:05:13] Ethan: I'll coordinate the SE deep dive — propose week of 4/20 — and I'll bring network runbook and perf tooling.
[00:05:20] Sam: Works for me.
[00:05:22] Janelle: My team will review the security pack; I might have follow-up on data deletion APIs.
[00:05:27] Maya: Noted. We'll include data deletion procedures.
[00:05:30] Victor: On pricing — can you send Dedicated reserved capacity pricing and an example unit-cost breakdown?
[00:05:36] Maya: Yes, I'll send a pricing sheet and a sample cost model for your traffic assumptions. We'll include token-level and per-request breakdown and the impact of batching/quantization.
[00:05:45] Dr. Laura Kim: Any gotchas or common pitfalls?
[00:05:48] Ethan: Common things: forgot to sanitize training/prompts for PHI if running evals; not setting up VPC early enough which delays provisioning; and expecting on-hosted latency without Dedicated sizing. We'll flag those.
[00:06:00] (background noise)
[00:06:03] Maya: Quick check — legal/procurement involvement?
[00:06:06] Victor: Legal will need the contract and security attachments. Procurement will join when we get Dedicated pricing.
[00:06:11] Maya: We'll send draft contract language and the security pack.
[00:06:14] Dr. Laura Kim: Great. Anything else on integrations? Sam?
[00:06:17] Sam: We'll need a short runbook for error handling — retries, fallbacks, and how to handle model degradations.
[00:06:22] Ethan: We have a recommended retry/backoff policy and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants; we'll include that in the runbook.
[00:06:29] Janelle: For auditability we'll want request IDs surfaced in logs and ability to correlate user IDs.
[00:06:34] Ravi: Request IDs are included in our logging; we can map to user identifiers if you supply the mapping fields.
[00:06:39] Maya: Ok team — let's recap action items quickly. Ethan?
[00:06:43] Ethan: I'll schedule the SE deep dive and share perf test template.
[00:06:46] Maya: I'll send the onboarding checklist, security pack, SSO guide, and pricing sheet.
[00:06:50] Sam: We'll provide staging access details and a sanitized prompt set.
[00:06:54] Janelle: I'll return the compliance answers and SOC2 checklist comments.
[00:06:58] Victor: Procurement will await the pricing and contract.
[00:07:01] Maya: Awesome. Any other questions?
[00:07:03] Dr. Laura Kim: No, thank you — excited to get started.
[00:07:07] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email with next steps and calendar invites.
[00:07:12] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription imperfections and speaker attributions may be approximate.
